---
title: "Day 22 demo: measure a TLC plate"
---

**Question:** what does an Rf calculation tell you, and what information is
lost if the solvent front was not recorded?

Allow **7 minutes**: predict for 2, adjust the plate for 3, then explain the
limits for 2. Distances are supplied hypothetical teaching measurements.

```{=html}
<section class="chem-demo" id="day22" aria-label="TLC spot and solvent-front geometry with Rf and co-migration controls">
<p>Enable JavaScript to vary distances from the origin and inspect the TLC ratio.</p>
</section>
<script src="../interactives/core.js"></script>
<script src="../interactives/applications.js"></script>
```

## Predict

Rf is spot-centre distance divided by solvent-front distance, **both measured
from the same origin**. Predict the value for 3.20 cm and 5.0 cm. Predict the
value for a spot halfway to the front and state its units.

## Explore

1. Change front and spot distances. Follow the geometrical plate as well as
   the reported ratio. The spot control stays between origin and front.
2. Use **Spot halfway to front** at more than one front distance.
3. Select **Front unrecorded**. Explain why spot height alone is insufficient.
4. Compare one known component with **two components with the same retention**.
   Can the visible plate distinguish those scenarios?

## Explain and check

$Rf=3.20/5.0=0.64$. A halfway spot gives **0.5**, independent of the numerical
front distance. The ratio is dimensionless. Without an actual recorded front,
the denominator is unknown and the tool correctly declines to invent an Rf.

Two components can co-migrate and produce the same visible feature. The
composition selector **supplies** a counterexample; the plate alone did not
measure that component count. One spot therefore does not prove purity.

## Model limits

Rf depends on stationary phase, eluent and other conditions, so matching
retention is not a unique identity code. Detection can also miss components.
Use matched conditions and appropriate independent structural/composition
evidence. The geometric model does not simulate molecular adsorption or
provide operating instructions. See the [local practical evidence guide](../reference/practical.qmd).
